question: In which of the following cities of Manipur is the Jawaharlal Nehru Manipur Dance Academy located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Imphal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Jawaharlal Nehru Manipur Dance Academy (JNMDA) is located in Imphal, the capital of Manipur. (जवाहरलाल नेहरू मणिपुर नृत्य अकादमी — इंफाल)

 

• It functions under the Department of Art and Culture, Government of Manipur, and imparts training in classical Manipuri dance and its allied forms such as Raas Leela.

 

• It was set up to preserve, promote and popularise the traditional dance and performing-arts heritage of the state.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Manipuri dance is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, marked by graceful, fluid movements and themes drawn from Vaishnavism.

 

• Imphal is also home to institutions such as the Manipur State Kala Akademi and the historic Govindajee Temple, both central to the state's cultural life.

 

NOTE

 

• Ukhrul (Option 2): A hill district of Manipur, home to the Tangkhul Naga tribe; it does not house the JNMDA.

 

• Chandel (Option 3): A border district of Manipur adjoining Myanmar; the academy is not located here.

 

• Thoubal (Option 4): A district in the Imphal Valley; the JNMDA is located in Imphal city, not Thoubal.

question: By which of the following state governments is the Tansen Music Festival organised?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh Government.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Tansen Music Festival (Tansen Samaroh) is organised every year by the Government of Madhya Pradesh at Gwalior. (तानसेन संगीत समारोह — मध्य प्रदेश सरकार)

 

• It is held near the tomb (mazar) of Tansen in Gwalior and commemorates the legendary musician Mian Tansen, one of the Navratnas (nine gems) of Emperor Akbar's court.

 

• It is one of the oldest classical music festivals in India, showcasing Hindustani classical music through performances by renowned vocalists and instrumentalists.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tansen is credited with composing several ragas, including Miyan ki Todi, Miyan ki Malhar and Darbari Kanada.

 

• The Madhya Pradesh government also confers the National Tansen Samman on eminent classical musicians during this festival.

 

NOTE

 

• Maharashtra Government (Option 1): Known for events like the Sawai Gandharva Bhimsen Mahotsav (Pune), not the Tansen festival.

 

• Rajasthan Government (Option 3): Hosts festivals such as the Pushkar Mela, unrelated to the Tansen Samaroh.

 

• Uttar Pradesh Government (Option 4): Hosts events like the Taj Mahotsav (Agra); it does not organise the Tansen Music Festival.

question: Which of the following places is related to Gandhi’s Satyagraha of the year 1917?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Champaran.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917, in Bihar, was Mahatma Gandhi's first Satyagraha movement in India. (चंपारण सत्याग्रह — 1917, बिहार)

 

• It was launched on behalf of indigo cultivators who were being forced by British planters under the Tinkathia system to grow indigo on a portion of their land.

 

• Gandhi was assisted in Champaran by leaders such as Rajendra Prasad, Anugrah Narayan Sinha and J.B. Kripalani.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kheda Satyagraha (1918), Gujarat, followed Champaran and was over remission of land revenue due to crop failure.

 

• The Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918) concerned a dispute between mill owners and workers over wages, while the Bardoli Satyagraha (1928), led by Vallabhbhai Patel, was against an unjust hike in land revenue.

 

NOTE

 

• Kheda (Option 1): Site of the 1918 Satyagraha over revenue remission, not the 1917 movement.

 

• Ahmedabad (Option 2): Site of the 1918 mill workers' strike, not the 1917 Satyagraha.

 

• Bardoli (Option 4): Site of the 1928 Satyagraha led by Vallabhbhai Patel, over a decade after 1917.

question: Hubbardia heptaneuron, which has become endangered, is a species of which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Grass.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hubbardia heptaneuron is a critically endangered species of grass (family Poaceae), endemic to India. (हबार्डिया हेप्टान्यूरॉन — घास की संकटाग्रस्त प्रजाति)

 

• It is a monotypic genus, meaning Hubbardia has only this single species, and it is known to grow on wet, rocky surfaces near waterfalls, notably around the Western Ghats in Maharashtra.

 

• Habitat loss and disturbance of its rocky-waterfall habitat have pushed the species to the brink of extinction.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other critically endangered Indian plant species include Ceropegia species and members of the genus Sirachne, several of which also grow in the Western Ghats' rock-outcrop ecosystems.

 

• The Western Ghats are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the world's eight biodiversity hotspots.

 

NOTE

 

• Bamboo (Option 2): Bamboo species belong to the same broader grass family but Hubbardia heptaneuron itself is not a bamboo.

 

• Tiger (Option 3): The tiger is an endangered animal, not a plant/grass species.

 

• Crane (Option 4): Cranes are endangered birds (e.g. the Siberian Crane), unrelated to Hubbardia heptaneuron.

question: Which of the following is in geographical proximity to Sri Lanka?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only Karaikal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Karaikal, one of the four regions of the Union Territory of Puducherry, lies on the Coromandel (south-eastern) coast of Tamil Nadu, in geographical proximity to Sri Lanka across the Palk Strait/Bay of Bengal. (कराईकल — श्रीलंका के निकट)

 

• The Union Territory of Puducherry comprises four non-contiguous regions: Puducherry and Karaikal in Tamil Nadu, Yanam in Andhra Pradesh, and Mahe in Kerala.

 

• Yanam lies on India's east coast but much farther north (near the Godavari delta in Andhra Pradesh), while Mahe lies on the west coast (Kerala) facing the Arabian Sea — neither is close to Sri Lanka.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The nearest Indian points to Sri Lanka are around Dhanushkodi and Rameswaram (Tamil Nadu), connected historically to Sri Lanka's Talaimannar by the chain of shoals called Adam's Bridge (Ram Setu).

 

• Puducherry became a Union Territory of India in 1963, after being a French colonial possession.

 

NOTE

 

• Karaikal and Yanam (Option 2): Incorrect because Yanam, on the Andhra coast, is not geographically close to Sri Lanka.

 

• Mahe (Option 3): Located on India's west coast (Kerala), facing away from Sri Lanka.

 

• Only Yanam (Option 4): Incorrect, as Yanam is far from Sri Lanka while Karaikal is the region actually in its proximity.

question: Which Five-Year Plan primarily focused on the 'Garibi Hatao' initiative?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fifth Five-Year Plan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974–79) had 'Garibi Hatao' (removal of poverty) and attainment of self-reliance as its central objectives. (गरीबी हटाओ — पांचवीं पंचवर्षीय योजना)

 

• The slogan 'Garibi Hatao' was popularised by Indira Gandhi during the 1971 Lok Sabha election campaign and was subsequently made the guiding objective of this Plan.

 

• The Plan also introduced programmes like the Minimum Needs Programme aimed at improving living standards of the poor.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Fifth Plan was terminated one year early (in 1978) by the Janata Party government, which replaced it with a rolling plan.

 

• It was formulated under the National Development Council with D.P. Dhar as the architect of its initial draft.

 

NOTE

 

• Sixth Five-Year Plan (Option 1): (1980–85) Focused on infrastructure, poverty alleviation via the IRDP, and technological self-reliance, but the 'Garibi Hatao' slogan itself originated with the Fifth Plan.

 

• Fourth Five-Year Plan (Option 2): (1969–74) Focused on the twin objectives of growth with stability and progress towards self-reliance, before 'Garibi Hatao' became the formal Plan objective.

 

• Third Five-Year Plan (Option 4): (1961–66) Focused on making the economy self-reliant, particularly through agriculture and industry (steel plants).

question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about the Directive Principles of State Policy?
option_1: They promote welfare of individuals. Hence, they are personal and individualistic.
option_2: These have moral and political sanctions.
option_3: They aim at establishing social and economic democracy in the country.
option_4: They are positive, as they require the State to do certain things.
solution_text:
The correct answer is They promote welfare of individuals. Hence, they are personal and individualistic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs), contained in Part IV (Articles 36–51) of the Constitution, aim at the welfare of the community as a whole, not merely of individuals — so calling them 'personal and individualistic' is incorrect. (राज्य के नीति निर्देशक तत्व — सामूहिक कल्याण)

 

• DPSPs are essentially social and collective in nature, directing the State towards establishing socio-economic democracy, unlike Fundamental Rights, which are more individualistic and justiciable.

 

• DPSPs are non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts) but carry moral and political sanction, and are positive in nature as they require the State to take affirmative action.

 

• Statements 2, 3 and 4 correctly describe these features of the DPSPs, making them true statements — leaving Statement 1 as the incorrect one.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The DPSPs were borrowed from the Irish Constitution, which had in turn borrowed the concept from Spain.

 

• They aim to establish a 'Welfare State' in India by combining socialist, Gandhian, and liberal-intellectual principles.

 

NOTE

 

• These have moral and political sanctions (Option 2): Correct — DPSPs cannot be enforced by courts but their violation invites political/electoral consequences.

 

• They aim at establishing social and economic democracy in the country (Option 3): Correct — this is a core purpose of the DPSPs.

 

• They are positive, as they require the State to do certain things (Option 4): Correct — unlike the largely negative Fundamental Rights, DPSPs positively direct the State to act.

question: After the death of Humayun, the 13 year-old Akbar was coronated in 1556 at Kalanaur in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• After Humayun's sudden death in 1556, his 13-year-old son Akbar was crowned emperor at Kalanaur, a town in present-day Gurdaspur district, Punjab. (कालानौर, पंजाब — अकबर का राज्याभिषेक)

 

• Akbar's regent and guardian at the time of coronation was Bairam Khan, who effectively administered the empire during the early years of Akbar's reign.

 

• Akbar went on to rule from 1556 to 1605, expanding and consolidating the Mughal Empire.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Humayun died in 1556 after falling from the stairs of his library, Sher Mandal, in Delhi.

 

• Akbar later defeated Hemu in the Second Battle of Panipat (1556) to secure the Mughal throne.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajasthan (Option 1): Not the site of Akbar's coronation, though Akbar later fought major battles here, such as the Siege of Chittorgarh.

 

• Gujarat (Option 2): Annexed by Akbar in 1572-73, long after his 1556 coronation.

 

• Bengal (Option 3): Conquered later during Akbar's reign; unrelated to his coronation.

question: The climate of a place is NOT affected by which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Type of soil.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Climate is chiefly influenced by factors such as latitude/location, relief (altitude), and distance from the sea (continentality); the type of soil, by contrast, is largely a product of climate, not a determinant of it. (जलवायु के नियामक — मृदा का प्रकार नहीं)

 

• Location (latitude) determines the amount of solar insolation received, directly affecting temperature and hence climate.

 

• Relief (altitude/mountain ranges) affects temperature and can block or channel moisture-bearing winds, as the Himalayas do for the monsoon.

 

• Distance from the sea determines the degree of continentality — coastal areas have more moderate climates than interior regions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major controls of climate include ocean currents, prevailing winds, and pressure belts.

 

• Soil formation (pedogenesis), conversely, is itself influenced by climate, along with parent rock, vegetation, and topography.

 

NOTE

 

• Relief (Option 1): A genuine determinant of climate through its effect on temperature and rainfall patterns.

 

• Location (Option 3): A genuine determinant of climate, as latitude governs the angle and duration of sunlight received.

 

• Distance from the sea (Option 4): A genuine determinant of climate through the moderating effect of maritime influence.

question: In which musical note did Newland put the metals Co and Ni with halogens?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Do.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Newlands' Law of Octaves (1865), elements were arranged in order of increasing atomic mass, and every eighth element showed properties similar to the first, resembling the octave of Western musical notes (Do, Re, Mi, Fa, Sol, La, Ti). (न्यूलैंड्स का अष्टक नियम — “डू” स्वर)

 

• A major limitation of this law was that it only held for lighter elements, forcing Newlands to place two elements in the same slot in some cases.

 

• Cobalt (Co) and Nickel (Ni) were placed together with the halogens (F, Cl, Br, I) under the note 'Do', even though their chemical properties are entirely different from halogens.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Newlands' Law of Octaves worked reasonably well only up to calcium; beyond that, elements did not fit the pattern.

 

• The law's shortcomings were later overcome by Mendeleev's Periodic Table (1869), which grouped elements by atomic mass while leaving gaps for undiscovered elements.

 

NOTE

 

• Fa (Option 1), Re (Option 3) and Mi (Option 4): These are other notes of Newlands' octave scale, but Co and Ni were specifically grouped under 'Do', not any of these.

question: Which of the following is NOT correct with regards to the history of calculating National Income (NI) in India?
option_1: First attempt to compute NI was made by Dadabhai Naoroji.
option_2: First official attempt to compute NI was made by PC Mahalanobis.
option_3: Dadabhai Naoroji divided the Indian economy into two parts: primary sector and secondary sector.
option_4: First scientific method to compute NI was used by Dr VKRV Rao.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dadabhai Naoroji divided the Indian economy into two parts: primary sector and secondary sector.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji, in his 1867 book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India', made the first attempt to estimate India's national income, but he divided the economy into agricultural and non-agricultural sectors, not 'primary and secondary sector' as stated. (दादाभाई नौरोजी — राष्ट्रीय आय का प्रथम अनुमान)

 

• The first official attempt to compute national income in India was indeed made under P.C. Mahalanobis through the National Income Committee (1949), set up by the Government of India.

 

• Dr V.K.R.V. Rao applied the first scientific method for computing national income in India, publishing his estimates in 1931 using a combination of the product and income methods.

 

• Since Statements 1, 2 and 4 are factually correct, Statement 3 is the incorrect one, making it the answer to this 'NOT correct' question.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Currently, national income estimates in India are prepared by the National Statistical Office (NSO), under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

 

• India shifted its base year for national income calculation to 2011-12 as part of methodological revisions.

 

NOTE

 

• First attempt to compute NI was made by Dadabhai Naoroji (Option 1): Correct statement, not the answer sought.

 

• First official attempt to compute NI was made by PC Mahalanobis (Option 2): Correct statement, not the answer sought.

 

• First scientific method to compute NI was used by Dr VKRV Rao (Option 4): Correct statement, not the answer sought.

question: According to the Indian Railways (2019-2020), which state has the largest railway track in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Indian Railways data (2019-20), Uttar Pradesh has the largest railway route length/track among Indian states. (उत्तर प्रदेश — सर्वाधिक रेल मार्ग लंबाई)

 

• This is largely because Uttar Pradesh is India's most populous state with a large geographical area, and it hosts major railway junctions and zones, including parts of Northern Railway, North Eastern Railway and North Central Railway.

 

• Key railway hubs in the state include Lucknow, Kanpur, Prayagraj, Varanasi and Gorakhpur (headquarters of the North Eastern Railway).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Indian Railways is one of the largest railway networks in the world, organised into 17-plus zones, headquartered in New Delhi.

 

• The Indian Railways was established in 1853, when the first passenger train ran between Bombay (Mumbai) and Thane.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab (Option 1), Haryana (Option 2) and Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): All have significant railway networks, but none matches Uttar Pradesh's total route length as per 2019-20 data.

question: Which government honoured a distinguished percussionist named Pandit Anindo Chatterjee with the Banga Vibhushan Award in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is West Bengal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Anindo Chatterjee, an eminent tabla maestro, was honoured with the Banga Bibhushan (Banga Vibhushan) Award by the Government of West Bengal in 2022. (बंग विभूषण सम्मान — पश्चिम बंगाल सरकार)

 

• The Banga Bibhushan is the highest civilian award of the State of West Bengal, conferred for outstanding contribution in fields such as art, literature, science, sports and public service.

 

• Anindo Chatterjee belongs to the renowned Farrukhabad gharana of tabla playing and is celebrated for his solo and accompaniment performances.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Banga Bibhushan awards are usually conferred around West Bengal's Foundation Day celebrations by the state government.

 

• Anindo Chatterjee has earlier also been associated with prestigious recognitions in the field of Indian classical percussion music.

 

NOTE

 

• Assam (Option 1): Confers its own state honours but did not award Anindo Chatterjee the Banga Vibhushan.

 

• Tripura (Option 2): Not the awarding state; the Banga Bibhushan is a West Bengal state honour.

 

• Jharkhand (Option 4): Has no connection with the Banga Bibhushan Award.

question: Which of the following festivals is celebrated as the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gurpurab.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gurpurab (Guru Nanak Gurpurab / Prakash Utsav) celebrates the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev, the founder of Sikhism, and falls on Kartik Purnima. (गुरुपर्व — गुरु नानक देव जयंती)

 

• Guru Nanak Dev was the first of the ten Sikh Gurus, born in 1469 at Talwandi (now Nankana Sahib, Pakistan).

 

• The festival is marked by Akhand Path (continuous recitation of the Guru Granth Sahib), processions called Nagar Kirtan, and community meals (langar) at gurdwaras worldwide.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Golden Temple, Amritsar, sees especially grand Gurpurab celebrations, including illuminations and fireworks.

 

• Guru Nanak Dev propagated the principles of one God, equality, and honest living, and is revered across faiths.

 

NOTE

 

• Hola Mohalla (Option 1): A Sikh festival held at Anandpur Sahib, a day after Holi, showcasing martial arts — not linked to Guru Nanak's birth.

 

• Baisakhi (Option 2): Marks the harvest festival and the formation of the Khalsa Panth by Guru Gobind Singh in 1699, not Guru Nanak's birth anniversary.

 

• Chappar Mela (Option 4): A fair held in Punjab in honour of Guga Pir (Gugga Ji), unrelated to Guru Nanak Dev.

question: Who was appointed as India’s 28th Controller General of Accounts (CGA) in March 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is SS Dubey.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Shri S.S. Dubey took charge as India's 28th Controller General of Accounts (CGA), Ministry of Finance, in March 2023. (एस.एस. दुबे — 28वें लेखा महानियंत्रक)

 

• The Controller General of Accounts (CGA) is the apex accounting authority of the Central Government, functioning under the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance.

 

• The CGA is responsible for establishing and maintaining a technically sound management accounting system, and for preparing the monthly and annual accounts of the Union Government.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The office of the CGA was created in 1976 as part of the departmentalisation of government accounts.

 

• Officers of the Indian Civil Accounts Service (ICAS) typically head this office as CGA.

 

NOTE

 

• Arun Goel (Option 1): Was appointed as an Election Commissioner of India, not CGA.

 

• Praveen Sharma (Option 2): Not associated with the office of CGA in this appointment.

 

• Vikram Devdutt (Option 3): Not the 28th CGA; unrelated to this appointment.

question: The Parliament passed the Marine Aids to Navigation Bill, 2021 to repeal and replace which of the following Acts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Lighthouse Act, 1927.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Marine Aids to Navigation Act, 2021 was passed by Parliament to repeal and replace the century-old Lighthouse Act, 1927. (समुद्री नौवहन सहायता अधिनियम 2021 — लाइटहाउस अधिनियम 1927 निरस्त)

 

• It modernises the regulatory framework governing lighthouses and other 'aids to navigation' such as buoys, beacons, and Vessel Traffic Services (VTS), extending India's jurisdiction to its Exclusive Economic Zone.

 

• The Act is administered by the Directorate General of Lighthouses and Lightships (DGLL), under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Act also provides for the establishment of a Marine Aids to Navigation Fund and enhanced training standards for related technical personnel.

 

• India has over 190 lighthouses along its coastline, several of which are now being developed for tourism under the government's lighthouse tourism initiative.

 

NOTE

 

• The Dangerous Machines (Regulation) Act, 1983 (Option 1): Deals with regulation of dangerous machines to protect workers; unrelated to navigation.

 

• The Personal Injuries (Emergency Provisions) Act, 1962 (Option 2): Deals with compensation for personal injuries during emergencies; unrelated to navigation.

 

• The Dourine Act, 1910 (Option 4): An old law relating to a contagious disease of horses (dourine); unrelated to navigation.

question: Which of the following is a non-perishable food?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pulses.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pulses are non-perishable foods — in their dried form they can be stored for long periods without refrigeration or spoiling. (गैर-नश्वर खाद्य पदार्थ — दालें)

 

• Perishable foods, such as meat, milk and curds, contain high moisture and nutrients that support rapid microbial growth, causing them to spoil quickly without refrigeration or preservation.

 

• Non-perishable foods like pulses, grains and cereals have low moisture content, which inhibits microbial activity and allows for long shelf life.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other common non-perishable foods include cereals, dry fruits, sugar, salt and dried spices.

 

• Preservation methods like drying, salting, canning and refrigeration are used to extend the shelf life of otherwise perishable foods.

 

NOTE

 

• Meat (Option 2): A highly perishable food that spoils quickly without refrigeration due to its high protein and moisture content.

 

• Curds (Option 3): A perishable dairy product that sours and spoils within a short time if not refrigerated.

 

• Milk (Option 4): A highly perishable food, prone to rapid bacterial spoilage without refrigeration or pasteurisation.

question: How many awards were presented at the National Sports and Adventure Awards-2022 ceremony held at Rashtrapati Bhavan on 30 November 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 44.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A total of 44 awards were presented at the National Sports and Adventure Awards-2022 ceremony held at Rashtrapati Bhavan on 30 November 2022, presented by President Droupadi Murmu. (राष्ट्रीय खेल एवं साहसिक पुरस्कार 2022 — 44 पुरस्कार)

 

• The awards spanned categories including the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award, Arjuna Awards, Dronacharya Awards, Dhyan Chand Awards (Lifetime Achievement), Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puruskar, the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad (MAKA) Trophy, and the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award-2021.

 

• These awards recognise excellence in sporting achievement, coaching, sports promotion by organisations, and outstanding adventure activities such as mountaineering and exploration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award is India's highest sporting honour, renamed in 2021 after hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand.

 

• The Maulana Abul Kalam Azad (MAKA) Trophy is awarded to the best overall performing university in inter-university tournaments.

 

NOTE

 

• 32, 52 and 28 (Options 1, 3 and 4): These figures do not match the actual total of 44 awards presented at the 2022 ceremony.

question: Which Governor-General of British India helped Raja Ram Mohan Roy legally abolish the sati practice?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord William Bentinck.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lord William Bentinck, Governor-General of India (1828–35), worked with social reformer Raja Ram Mohan Roy to legally abolish the practice of Sati through the Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829. (सती प्रथा उन्मूलन — लॉर्ड विलियम बेंटिंक, 1829)

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy, founder of the Brahmo Samaj, campaigned extensively against the practice of Sati, providing the social reform momentum behind the legislation.

 

• This regulation declared the practice of Sati (immolation of a widow on her husband's funeral pyre) illegal and punishable in courts of law within British-administered territories.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lord William Bentinck also introduced English as the medium of higher education in India, following Macaulay's Minute (1835).

 

• He is also known for suppressing the practice of Thuggee with the help of Sir William Sleeman.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Ripon (Option 1): Known for the Ilbert Bill and local self-government reforms; not associated with the abolition of Sati.

 

• Lord Curzon (Option 2): Known for the Partition of Bengal (1905); not associated with the abolition of Sati.

 

• Lord Cornwallis (Option 3): Known for the Permanent Settlement (1793); served decades before the abolition of Sati.

question: When was the 1st Asian Kabaddi Championship held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1980.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 1st Asian Kabaddi Championship was held in 1980 in India, under the aegis of the Asian Kabaddi Federation (AKF). (प्रथम एशियाई कबड्डी चैंपियनशिप — 1980)

 

• India has traditionally dominated this tournament, winning most editions of the Asian Kabaddi Championship since its inception.

 

• Kabaddi, a contact team sport of Indian origin, was included in the Asian Games for the first time at Beijing 1990.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kabaddi is the national game of Bangladesh and is also popularly played in Iran, Pakistan, Nepal and other South Asian countries.

 

• The Pro Kabaddi League (PKL), launched in 2014, significantly boosted the sport's popularity in India.

 

NOTE

 

• 1970, 1985 and 1975 (Options 1, 2 and 4): These years do not correspond to the first edition of the Asian Kabaddi Championship, which was held in 1980.

question: The decomposition of gaseous Ammonia on a hot platinum surface is a _______________ order reaction at high pressure.
solution_text:
The correct answer is zero.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The thermal decomposition of ammonia (NH₃) on a hot platinum surface is a zero order reaction at high pressure. (अमोनिया का अपघटन, प्लैटिनम सतह — शून्य कोटि अभिक्रिया)

 

• At high pressure, the platinum surface becomes completely covered (saturated) with NH₃ molecules, so the rate of decomposition no longer depends on the concentration of ammonia — making it zero order.

 

• In a zero order reaction, the rate of reaction is independent of the concentration of the reactant, i.e., Rate = k[NH₃]⁰ = k, a constant.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• At low pressure, however, the same reaction becomes a first order reaction, since the platinum surface is not fully saturated and the rate then depends on NH₃ concentration.

 

• Other classic examples of zero order reactions include the photochemical reaction between H₂ and Cl₂, and enzyme-catalysed reactions at high substrate concentration.

 

NOTE

 

• Two, three and one (Options 1, 3 and 4): Do not describe this reaction under high-pressure conditions, where the surface-saturation effect makes the reaction zero order, not second, third or first order.

question: Which of the following was the mascot of the FIH men’s Hockey World Cup – 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Olly.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Olly', an Olive Ridley turtle, was the official mascot of the FIH Men's Hockey World Cup 2023, held in Bhubaneswar and Rourkela, Odisha. (एफआईएच पुरुष हॉकी विश्व कप — शुभंकर “ऑली”)

 

• The mascot was chosen to spotlight Odisha's efforts in conserving Olive Ridley sea turtles, which nest in large numbers along the state's coast, notably at Gahirmatha.

 

• The tournament was won by Germany, who defeated Belgium in the final to claim their third Hockey World Cup title.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• This was the second consecutive edition of the Men's Hockey World Cup hosted by Odisha, after the 2018 edition held in Bhubaneswar.

 

• Odisha is home to the Kalinga Stadium (Bhubaneswar) and the Birsa Munda Hockey Stadium (Rourkela), both major venues for international hockey.

 

NOTE

 

• Jitu, Bheema and Asha (Options 1, 2 and 4): Not the actual mascot names; the official mascot of the 2023 tournament was 'Olly'.

question: The Indian Constitution has established _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is independent judicial system.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Constitution establishes a single, integrated judiciary that is independent of the Legislature and the Executive, so as to safeguard the rule of law and protect citizens' Fundamental Rights. (स्वतंत्र न्यायपालिका — संविधान द्वारा स्थापित)

 

• Judicial independence is secured through provisions such as security of tenure for judges, fixed salaries charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, and restrictions on the discussion of judicial conduct in the Legislature.

 

• Unlike the USA, which has a dual/federal judicial system with separate hierarchies of federal and state courts, India follows a single integrated system of courts headed by the Supreme Court, with High Courts and subordinate courts below it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Supreme Court of India was inaugurated on 28 January 1950, replacing the Federal Court of India.

 

• Articles 124 to 147 of the Constitution deal with the organisation, jurisdiction and powers of the Supreme Court.

 

NOTE

 

• Partial judicial system (Option 1): Not a recognised constitutional feature; India's judiciary is described as independent, not partial.

 

• Dual judicial system (Option 2): Incorrect — India has a single integrated judicial system, unlike federations such as the USA with dual/parallel hierarchies.

 

• Plural judicial system (Option 4): Not the constitutional description; India's courts form one unified hierarchy, not a plural/multiple system.

question: Which organisms are classified as Aves?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Birds.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Aves is the taxonomic class comprising all birds, within the animal kingdom (Kingdom Animalia, Phylum Chordata). (एवीज़ वर्ग — पक्षी)

 

• Birds are characterised by features such as feathers, beaks without teeth, forelimbs modified into wings, and being warm-blooded (endothermic).

 

• Members of Aves typically lay hard-shelled eggs and have a four-chambered heart, along with a lightweight skeleton adapted for flight.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ornithology is the branch of zoology dealing with the study of birds.

 

• The Ostrich is the largest living bird, while the Bee Hummingbird is the smallest.

 

NOTE

 

• Fishes (Option 1): Belong to classes such as Pisces/Osteichthyes and Chondrichthyes, not Aves.

 

• Frogs (Option 2): Belong to class Amphibia, not Aves.

 

• Snakes (Option 3): Belong to class Reptilia, not Aves.

question: Mahabalipuram emerged as an important centre of temple architecture under which of the following kingdoms of south India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pallava.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram), in Tamil Nadu, emerged as a major centre of temple architecture under the Pallava dynasty, especially during the reign of Narasimhavarman I ('Mamalla') in the 7th century CE. (महाबलीपुरम — पल्लव वंश)

 

• It is renowned for its rock-cut Rathas (chariot-shaped monolithic temples), the Shore Temple, and bas-relief carvings such as 'Arjuna's Penance' (Descent of the Ganga).

 

• Mahabalipuram was a flourishing port town under the Pallavas, facilitating maritime trade and cultural exchange with Southeast Asia.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1984.

 

• The Pallava capital was at Kanchipuram, another major centre of temple architecture, notably the Kailasanathar Temple.

 

NOTE

 

• Chola (Option 2): Known for temples like the Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur, a later South Indian dynasty distinct from the Pallavas.

 

• Chera (Option 3): A dynasty of ancient Kerala/south-west India, not associated with Mahabalipuram's temple architecture.

 

• Chalukya (Option 4): Known for temples at Badami, Pattadakal and Aihole in Karnataka, a different region and dynasty from Mahabalipuram.
